data.gender_notes: Parshant is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit word 'Parshva' which means 'Supreme Lord'. The name Parshant is a revered name in Hindu mythology and symbolizes power, wisdom, and divine protection. The name Parshant carries the meaning “Supreme Lord” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Parshant usually hope their child will grow to embody supreme lord and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Parshant total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: In traditional Hindu society, the name Parshant signifies a strong connection to the ancient Vedic texts and the rich Hindu cultural heritage.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Parshant is believed to invoke the blessings of Lord Parshurama, the sixth avatar of Lord Vishnu, who is considered the embodiment of strength, courage, and martial prowess.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Parshant: The radiant one, embodying inner strength and wisdom, illuminating the path towards self-realization.

historical_references.reference: Parshant was a sage mentioned in the ancient Hindu scripture, the Mahabharata. He was one of the seven sages (Saptarishis) who lived on Mount Meru, the abode of the gods.
historical_references.context: Mahabharata is an ancient Sanskrit epic that is one of the two major sources of Hindu mythology and Indian philosophy. It is believed to have been composed between 400 BCE and 200 BCE.

historical_references.reference: Parshant was also the name of a famous Jain Tirthankara, the 23rd in the current cycle of 24 Tirthankaras. He lived around the 8th or 9th century BCE.
historical_references.context: Jainism is an ancient Indian religion that emphasizes nonviolence, self-control, and renunciation. Tirthankaras are believed to be the teachers who guide the souls to the right path of salvation.
